newsitem.title: USA: Georgia voters approve two bond issues, sales tax.
newsitem.headline: Georgia voters approve two bond issues, sales tax.

text.p: Voters in three Georgia counties approved two general obligation bond issues for schools and recreation and a local sales tax increase for a variety of projects, elections officials said Wednesday.

Richmond County voters approved a $115 million general obligation bond issue for schools. The measure passed with 62 percent of the votes for and 38 percent against, elections officials in Marietta said.
The school bond referendum was the county's first since 1988, when voters approved a $22.5 million issue for schools, and will add $98.80 per year to the property tax bill for a $100,000 home.
In Cobb County, voters approved a $30 million general obligation bond issue for recreation. The proposal passed with 64 percent of the votes for and 36 percent against.

Gwinnett County voters approved approved a once-cent sales tax increase to fund park, library and public safety projects. The measure passed with 84,928 yes votes, or 53.24 percent, and 74,577 no votes, or 46.7 percent, elections officials said.
The approval comes one year after Gwinnett County votes rejected a one-cent sales tax increase that would have raised $675 million for roads.
